Answer: C
Reason: The clinical history of a recent vertebroplasty combined with an intraoperative drop in end-tidal CO2 is highly suggestive of pulmonary embolism. The provided CT images (Figures 4a and 4b) clearly show hyperdense, radiopaque material within the pulmonary arteries, which is characteristic of cement embolism resulting from the leakage of polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) into the venous system during the procedure.
